code.pseudocode: A scalar is a single number, such as the area of one house.
List the features of one house in a fixed order. That ordered list is a vector.
The dimension of a vector is how many entries it has.
Put one vector per house on its own row. The table of rows is a matrix.

steps.label: Stack the vectors into a matrix

code.pseudocode: A row is one house. A column is one feature for every house.
code.python:
X = [[1200, 2, 10], [1800, 3, 4], [900, 1, 15]]
row = X[1]                  # house 2
column = [r[0] for r in X]  # every area
print(row, column)

steps.label: Pick a row and a column

code.pseudocode: Swap rows and columns: the first column becomes the first row.
A machine learning dataset is a matrix: one row per example and one column per feature.
code.python:
X = [[1200, 2, 10], [1800, 3, 4], [900, 1, 15]]
n_examples, n_features = len(X), len(X[0])
print(n_examples, n_features)

steps.label: See the dataset as a matrix
